I therefore retained m177 as an unresolved hypothesis rather than applying a global tail correction. The m80 outcomes at 1/1, 2/1, 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1 remain clustered near 5 to 8 mL, so the earlier steep-ratio hypothesis is now supported as a plateau hypothesis and the selected m80 points focus on loading-solvent-volume transfer. Recent large errors for m90, m94, m107, m117, m120, m135, m141, m146, m159, m193, m198, and m207 show that the remaining gain is concentrated in structure-specific high-retention surfaces, especially where V2 is much less predictable than V1.","batch_rationale":"The batch repairs several distinct failure regions while preserving scientifically meaningful local contrasts. m96, m159, m193, m207, m90, m94, and m107 receive paired or near-paired conditions to teach ratio and loading response. m80 supplies two plateau checks, while m31, m37, m72, m112, m117, m120, m128, m135, m141, m146, m188, m198, and m42 broaden supervision across halogenated aromatics, ethers, alcohols, heteroaromatics, esters, ketones, and multifunctional carbonyl compounds. Strong-solvent anchors and moderate-ratio interpolation points help keep the retrained model calibrated at both the low-volume boundary and the late-tail region. This combination targets measured failure repair, tests competing local response explanations, and adds reusable structure-condition labels likely to improve V1 and V2 generalization across the Row-distribution."}
